tagline: Leading zero-carbon energy provider through nuclear generation and state-sponsored programs
hero_kpi_rationale: Nuclear PTC revenue represents a structural and growing government revenue stream for eligible nuclear plants, reflecting federal policy support for decarbonized energy through 2032

kpis.name: Nuclear Production Tax Credit Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from transferable tax credits for nuclear power plants, up to $15 per MWh
kpis.description: Federal transferable tax credit available for eligible nuclear units from 2024 to 2032, subject to a phase-out schedule based on annual gross revenue thresholds
kpis.signal: Significant decline due to interaction with state-sponsored programs

kpis.name: Net Revenue from State-Sponsored Programs
kpis.explanation: Net revenue from state compensation programs (ZEC, CMC) after deduction of nuclear tax credit and contractual reimbursements
kpis.description: Net revenue from state compensation programs including Zero Emission Credits (ZEC) and Capacity Market Supply Contracts (CMC), net of refunds and transfers related to the nuclear tax credit
kpis.signal: Significant increase in net reimbursements due to the application of the nuclear tax credit

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Total amount paid in dividends per share over the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Annual total: dividends paid + share buybacks.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Share of net income distributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

risks.title: Credit Rating Downgrade
risks.score_rationale: A three-notch downgrade below investment grade (from BBB+/Baa1 to BB+/Ba1 or lower) would result in significantly higher financing costs, an estimated $2.7 billion in additional collateral requirements, and reduced access to capital markets

risks.title: Market Deterioration
risks.score_rationale: Market deterioration could lead to reduced energy demand and lower prices, negatively impacting the company's financial results. The company is exposed to market risks related to energy price fluctuations.

risks.title: Counterparty Credit Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is exposed to credit risks from counterparty non-performance, which could result in significant financial losses. The company has nuclear fuel supply contracts with Russian counterparties, which could be affected by economic sanctions.

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict regulations regarding nuclear safety and environmental protection, and regulatory changes could negatively impact financial performance. The company must comply with requirements from the NRC and other regulatory bodies.

risks.title: Liquidity Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company could face liquidity risks if it is unable to fund its operations and investments. Although the company has $7.4 billion of available capacity under its credit facilities and $3.6 billion in cash, significant acquisitions such as the Calpine transaction create substantial financing needs.

risks.title: Nuclear Decommissioning Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is responsible for decommissioning its nuclear plants, representing an asset retirement obligation of $12.9 billion as of December 31, 2025. Future costs depend on complex probabilistic models, cost escalation factors, and discount rates.
